questions.explain: Diagnostics: peak IOPS below 2,500 on gp2 → gp3 with no extra IOPS; BurstBalance frequently below 20% → hitting the burst ceiling; DiskQueueDepth regularly above 1.0 → storage is a real bottleneck needing more IOPS, not cost reduction. SQL Server: avg_read_latency_ms above 20ms signals storage pressure; cache hit ratio above 99% means the workload is memory-bound and gp3's baseline suffices.

questions.explain: The migration is an online operation with no downtime — applications stay connected; for Multi-AZ, the change applies to the standby first, then fails over (a brief 20–30 second failover) and applies to the former primary, so schedule during low-traffic periods if sensitive. If DiskQueueDepth climbs above 1.0 or latency rises after migration, increase provisioned IOPS with another modify call (takes effect in minutes).

questions.explain: io2 is warranted for: sustained high-concurrency write OLTP saturating gp3's 16,000 ceiling; large databases with full-scan analytics on the OLTP instance; latency-sensitive write patterns (e.g., Oracle redo contention — io2 guarantees single-digit-ms latency); and small volumes needing high IOPS where io2's 500:1 IOPS-to-GB ratio avoids oversized volumes. There is no reason to choose io1 for new deployments — io2 costs the same or less with higher durability.
options: io2 for sustained high-IOPS OLTP, latency-sensitive write workloads, or small volumes needing high IOPS (better IOPS-to-GB ratio); never choose io1 for new deployments
